metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent created a forward filter named 'Forward all emails to Gmail' targeting anonym-x2024@gmail.com. This variation requires a specific filter name 'Gmail Forward', adding a naming constraint to the original task.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open Message Filters dialog, type a custom filter name, set forward action with target email
metadata.explanation: Getter reads filter names and forward destination from msgFilterRules.dat. Metric awards 0.5 for a filter whose name contains 'gmail forward' (case-insensitive) and 0.5 for the forward destination matching anonym-x2024@gmail.com. Initial state scores 0.0. [Fixed: renamed functions from invalid 12-char suffix '70c637de0570' to correct 32-char MD5 'e2cb27642e2d718992a0ab3ec3b240f1' derived from task_id|variation_index]
fix_history: Fix 1: Renamed getter 'get_tb_named_forward_filter__70c637de0570' to 'get_tb_named_forward_filter__e2cb27642e2d718992a0ab3ec3b240f1' (invalid 12-char suffix replaced with correct 32-char MD5 of '9b7bc335-06b5-4cd3-9119-1a649c478509|1')
Fix 3: Updated evaluator.func and evaluator.result.type in task JSON to match new 32-char MD5 suffix
metadata.task_rationale: Harder variant of the source task: adds a naming constraint so the evaluator checks both the filter name and the forwarding destination, requiring the agent to follow an explicit naming instruction.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads msgFilterRules.dat and extracts filter names and forward destinations, covering the two primary requirements of the instruction.

Metric checks filter name via case-insensitive substring match ('gmail forward' in name) and forward destination via exact case-insensitive equality, which will work for the intended correct solution.
Initial state (no filters) correctly scores 0.0, providing negative-control resistance.

ISSUE: Filter name and forward destination are checked independently, not linked to the same filter. A filter named 'Gmail Forward' with a different action plus a separate filter forwarding to the correct email would incorrectly score 1.0.

ISSUE: The getter stores only the last forward actionValue across all filters. If multiple forwarding filters exist, only the last destination is checked, which may miss or misattribute the correct filter.
ISSUE: No account-scope verification — the getter searches all msgFilterRules.dat files without confirming the filter belongs to the anonym-x2024@outlook.com account.

ISSUE: No verification that the filter has 'Match all messages' condition — a filter with the correct name that only conditionally forwards emails (e.g., from specific senders) would still receive full credit.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Link filter name to forward destination within the getter by tracking (name, action, actionValue) tuples per filter block, then check in the metric that a single filter has BOTH the expected name and the correct forward destination.
Scope the search to the msgFilterRules.dat file under the anonym-x2024@outlook.com profile directory (e.g., filter paths containing the account identifier) to ensure account-level correctness.
Add a check in the getter for the filter's condition section (e.g., absence of condition lines or presence of 'match all' flag) to verify the filter applies to every incoming email.
